skill.name: sound-less-like-ai
skill.description: Rewrite text so it stops reading as machine-written, by naming the specific tells and removing them. Use when someone says a draft sounds like AI, sounds generic, sounds corporate, or asks to humanise or de-AI a piece of writing. Do not use it to help anyone pass off writing as human where being honest about authorship matters, such as academic work or disclosures.
skill.summary: Identify generic writing habits, remove filler, and rewrite drafts with concrete details and varied sentence rhythms.
skill.author: prateeks367

content.user_title: Rewrite Generic Drafts in a More Natural Voice
content.value_statement: Generic drafts often contain repetitive rhythms, vague claims, and unnecessary filler. This skill identifies those patterns and guides rewrites using concrete details and clearer phrasing.
actual_capabilities: Identify repetitive sentence rhythms, padding, generic vocabulary, and unsupported claims with quotes from the draft.
Remove filler and redundant statements before adding new material.
Ask for specific facts, experiences, or opinions to make writing more concrete.
Vary sentence lengths and preserve phrasing that reflects the writer.
When VoiceMOAT is connected, use voice profiles, voice similarity scoring, and deeper structural editing tools.
limitations: Cannot guarantee that a rewrite will pass an AI detector.
Does not help conceal authorship in academic submissions or disclosures.
Needs user-provided facts and personal details rather than inventing them.
VoiceMOAT personalization and scoring require a connected service and a Pro or Enterprise plan.

use_cases.title: Revise public updates
use_cases.description: Remove generic phrases from product updates and use supplied dates, numbers, and decisions to make the message specific.

use_cases.title: Edit article drafts
use_cases.description: Identify repetitive structures and filler, then revise an article while preserving the writer's opinions and factual claims.

use_cases.title: Clarify workplace messages
use_cases.description: Rewrite repetitive emails into direct messages and explain the changes so the writer can recognize similar patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite a short draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Make this draft less generic: [draft]. Quote the main problems, rewrite it, and explain the changes.

prompt_templates.title: Remove filler first
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this draft: [draft]. Identify padding and repeated ideas, then remove them without changing the meaning. Show before-and-after comparisons.

prompt_templates.title: Add grounded detail
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise [draft] for [audience] using these verified details: [facts]. Vary sentence lengths, preserve my opinion, and flag missing information instead of inventing it.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: revising an audience-specific article or update.

prompt_templates.title: Match a connected voice profile
prompt_templates.prompt: If VoiceMOAT is connected, use my voice profile to revise [draft] and score the result. Explain structural changes. Otherwise, ask for writing samples.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: personalizing a draft with an optional connector.

output_examples.input: Draft: It is important to note that our robust platform can help teams leverage seamless collaboration. Fact: Review time fell from five days to two.
output: Identified patterns: 'It is important to note' adds padding. 'Robust,' 'leverage,' and 'seamless' add vague claims.
Rewrite: Our platform reduced review time from five days to two.
Changes: Removed the introductory filler and replaced generic claims with the supplied result.

output_examples.input: Draft: The release improved reliability. The release improved performance. The release improved usability. Facts: We fixed two crashes and reduced load time to one second.
output: Identified pattern: Each sentence repeats 'The release improved' without supporting details.
Rewrite: We fixed two crashes in this release. Load time is now one second.
Changes: Removed the repeated structure and used supplied facts. Omitted the usability claim because no supporting detail was provided.

best_practices: Provide the draft, intended audience, and factual details that may be included.
Review quoted problems and before-and-after comparisons before accepting the rewrite.
Keep necessary authorship disclosures and verify every factual claim in the final text.
anti_patterns: Requesting a guaranteed AI detector pass.
Using rewrites to conceal authorship in academic work or required disclosures.
Adding invented numbers, experiences, or opinions to make a draft seem personal.

faq.question: What does this skill change?
faq.answer: It identifies repetitive rhythms, filler, generic vocabulary, and vague claims, then guides a rewrite and explains the edits.

faq.question: Does it guarantee a human authorship classification?
faq.answer: No. The skill explicitly rejects AI detector guarantees because detector results can be unreliable.

faq.question: Can I use it without VoiceMOAT?
faq.answer: Yes. The core editing guidance works without VoiceMOAT. Voice profiles, similarity scores, and deeper editing tools depend on the optional connector.

faq.question: What does the VoiceMOAT connector require?
faq.answer: The skill states that the connector needs a VoiceMOAT Pro or Enterprise plan.

faq.question: Will it invent personal details for my draft?
faq.answer: The workflow asks you for concrete details, experiences, or opinions. Provide accurate information and verify the resulting rewrite.

faq.question: Can it disguise AI authorship in academic work?
faq.answer: No. The skill refuses to conceal authorship where honesty matters, including academic submissions and disclosures.
